results.finding: Both readers describe the declared order: general to specific (callouts, bridge, thesis, figure, order paragraph, table, connections, Veldmark, start) with chapters in dependency order; neither marks any section's position unclear and neither would reorder sections. Points both readers raised about Tradeyard, the named people, 'paid effects', 'bump-price', 'the monolith' and 'contacts' concern terms on audience.already_knows (meet-veldmark, Part VI's paid effects and contact counts, Yardstick monolith) and are not material for the spec's reader.

results.quote: the data platform's metrics, experiments that need them and models that need both. Tenancy decides how all are shared
results.finding: Both readers re-read the sentence to find what 'both' refers to (metrics and experiments, or the event stream and metrics); reader B adds that 'all' in the next sentence is equally vague. The spec's order is sound; the prose obscures the dependency chain. Name the referents (e.g. 'models that need metrics and experiments'; 'how all of these capabilities are shared').

results.quote: starts 2027 with four messaging technologies, three warehouses, 146 production models
results.finding: Both readers paused on 'warehouses', which in a marketplace book can read as physical warehouses until the Data bullet resolves it. The ledger's own wording is 'three data warehouses'; one word fixes it.

results.quote:
listed in chapter order with each decision's date:
- *Events:* **Listing event contract v1** on Kafka (Confluent Cloud), live on 1 July 2027;
results.finding: The lead-in promises each decision's date but the first bullet gives a go-live date ('live on'), so both readers stopped to check whether the other dates are decision or go-live dates. Make the lead-in and the first bullet agree (e.g. 'with its date', or drop 'live on' if 1 July 2027 is the contract's date per the ledger).

results.quote: no peak calendar (a shared schedule of campaigns and heavy jobs) had flagged the clash. Ingrid Halvorsen's team
results.finding: Reader B had to connect the brown-out in the opening sentence to its answer in the last of eight bullets ('they answer the brown-out'). Reader A did not report this.

results.quote: a price test with the wrong sign
results.finding: Reader A had to work out that 'wrong sign' means the measured effect pointed the wrong way; it is clarified only by the bump-price bullet. Reader B did not report it. Previously recorded by the author as kept published text.

results.quote: Make the tenant first-class and market differences configuration
results.finding: Reader B found the 'make ... configuration' construction a garden path that is clear only on a second pass. (The 'tenant' part of the same sentence is judged under known_before_new.) Reader A did not report the construction.

results.quote: By the end of Part VII you can say, for any listing fact, where it is true, which copies hold it and how you would rebuild or erase them.
results.finding: Reader B found the closing promise narrower than the part: it speaks to events and copies, not SEO, experiments, models, tenancy or reliability. The draft states the spec's so_what as written, so the difficulty comes from the spec. Reader A did not report it; previously recorded by the author as not acted on.

results.quote: Make the tenant first-class and market differences configuration, with forks allowed only when they carry an expiry date.
results.finding: 'Tenant' is neither on audience.already_knows nor glossed where it first appears; the page explains it only in the Tenancy bullet near the end ('ten brand × country tenants'). Both flow readers report it as unexplained (B: 'I could not tell whether a tenant is a brand, a country or a customer'). Gloss at first use, e.g. 'the tenant (a brand in a country)'.

Every does_not_know term the page uses is glossed: staleness budget, interference-aware designs, decision tier, read model, extension points, error budgets, consumer registry, degradation ladder, peak calendar; journey objectives are glossed by 'user journey' (p03) and 'journey service level objectives' (reader A called 'journey' guessable). Outbox, envelope, schema compatibility and replay are not used. Paid effects, bump-price, contacts, Tradeyard, the named people and the monolith are on already_knows.
